title: Stakeholder Power-Interest Grid
description: Place stakeholders on a power-interest grid and justify a different engagement strategy for each quadrant.
creator: Systems Thinking in the Age of AI
author: Dan McCreary
subject: Systems Thinking in the Age of AI
Systems Design, Emerging Technology, and Practice
chapter_title: Systems Design, Emerging Technology, and Practice

educational.learningObjective: Given a set of stakeholders in a system-design scenario, the learner will classify each one by power and interest and justify a prioritized engagement strategy for each quadrant.
prerequisites: Has worked on a project with more than one interested party
learningOutcomes: Classify stakeholders by power and interest
Name an appropriate engagement strategy for each quadrant
Explain why a high-power low-interest stakeholder is the dangerous one
educational.assessmentOpportunity: Ask learners to justify one stakeholder's placement and to state the engagement strategy that follows from it.

pedagogical.interactionPattern: Draggable 2x2 matrix with attitude coding and scenario variation
pedagogical.instructionalStrategy: Classification with peer disagreement as the teaching mechanism
pedagogical.feedbackType: Live quadrant assignment as dots are dragged
misconceptionsAddressed: That the most vocal stakeholder is the most powerful one
That a stakeholder's position is fixed
discussionQuestions: Why is a high-power, low-interest stakeholder the one most likely to derail a project late?
Does attitude change the strategy, or only the effort required?
How often should a grid like this be redrawn?
